What makes this particularly frustrating is that I still wanted to use their technology. After realizing my mistake, I separately purchased the correct Grok Bot access and continue to use it. I am not trying to get their service for free — I paid for the product I actually wanted and simply requested a refund for the wrong, unused SuperGrok subscription immediately after purchasing it.  
Support then asked me to submit the refund information again, which I did. Despite this, I ended up in the same automated process again. [...] This is especially concerning for a company selling AI products intended for serious and business use. The technology itself may be interesting, and I actually wanted to continue using Grok Bot, but this experience has significantly reduced my confidence in the overall service. If a simple billing issue can become trapped in an endless AI loop with no meaningful human escalation, I have to question what happens when a genuinely serious problem occurs.  
I will update this review if xAI eventually resolves the issue. [...] ## Refund request stuck in an AI support loop
I wanted to give Grok and SuperGrok a serious try, but my experience with their customer support has made me seriously reconsider using their services for business.  
I accidentally purchased the wrong subscription — SuperGrok — when what I actually wanted was Grok Bot. I realized the mistake immediately, did not use the SuperGrok subscription, and requested a refund on the same day as the purchase. I received refund request PRO-103035.

results.title: Grok Bot (Ultra) unreliable for business use — credit balance load failure, Slack drops, router bot degradation under load, insufficient native memory/project/task tracking - Bug Reports - Cursor - Community Forum
results.content:
Today’s prompts look like they came during the billing problem I mentioned earlier, which the team has now mitigated. If Grok Bot still asks for credits after you restart the app, reply here and we’ll take another look.

Thanks for the clear breakdown, Collin

Good to know the request for letting people without a Cursor seat talk to a shared Bot in Slack is already being tracked. I think that would meaningfully increase business usage, since a lot of teams have staff or collaborators who don’t need full Cursor seats and just aren’t that technical, but still need to interact with the Bot through Slack. [...] These are reliability and capability gaps that make the product unsuitable for ongoing business use in its current state. Happy to provide more logs or high-level examples. [...] Slack Bot: Here are some concrete examples. All times are US Central (CT).

How we use it: our staff aren’t very technical, and Slack is how they reach our Grok Bot setup. Through our Slack bot “Pepe Silvia” they ask questions, and they also kick off workflows we’ve built on the back end. Those include writing and refreshing article drafts, building briefs from our research dashboard, approving or cancelling jobs, price rechecks, compliance checks and reports. Behind it is a shared “brain” of project files, rules and tracker data, plus about 14 agents that split the work. Staff never open Grok Bot. They just @mention Pepe in a work channel or reply in its thread, and the right agent does the job and posts back.
